subject: Prospective PhD applicant (Fall 2027): people's sense of control over AI that acts on their data
body:
Dear Professor Li,

I'm applying to the Khoury HCI PhD program for Fall 2027, and I'm writing because I'd like to work with you.

For four years I've been a product data analyst at a consumer fitness app. Last year we launched a feature that rewrites people's workout plans using their sleep, heart-rate, and activity data. By our metrics it was a success. But in the survey responses, roughly one in ten people said their plan had changed and they didn't know why, or asked how the app knew they'd slept badly. A couple had turned off health-data sharing. Those comments ended up folded into a single sentiment score, and I haven't stopped thinking about them.

I want to study what people think is happening when a system uses their own data to decide things for them, and what would make them feel they still have a say. Your COLM 2026 paper on autonomy and personalization in LLM agents is close to this. Its finding that handing control back to users at moments of risk changed how they felt about personalization connects directly to what I saw in those responses.

I have limited research experience, mostly an undergraduate HCI interview study and a usability test. I do have a lot of practice designing and analyzing experiments. Are you planning to take new PhD students for Fall 2027? If so, I'd be grateful for any chance to talk briefly.

Thank you for your time.

Best,
Riley Nakamura
riley.nakamura@example.com
